observed.text: The narration says, “that bridge is still marked in Smoots.”
The on-screen caption changes to “that bridge is still” and then “marked in Smoots.”
A real photo shows the word “SMOOTS” painted on the bridge surface.
The photo credit identifies “Harvard Bridge, Massachusetts · July 2024.”
The final photo remains substantially still from about 8.3s through 10.5s.

findings.viewer_understanding: The viewer understands that Smoot became the bridge’s named body-length unit and that markings remain on the bridge.
findings.predicted_reaction: The real-photo reveal lands, but a viewer who expected the actual bridge length after the repeated end-to-end measuring setup is left without that answer.
findings.weakness: The ending proves the markings exist but never gives the measured total. The setup repeatedly foregrounds measuring a whole bridge, so withholding the resulting number leaves the factual payoff incomplete.
alternatives: The intended payoff may be only that the markings survived nearly seventy years.
The short runtime may intentionally prioritize the surprising physical proof over the total measurement.
findings.proposed_repair: Add the final total as one concise line over the bridge photo before or alongside “marked in Smoots,” while retaining the real painted “SMOOTS” image as the closing proof.
keep_unchanged: Keep the 8.25s cut to the real bridge photo.
Keep the visible painted “SMOOTS” marking and source credit.
Keep the concise final statement that the bridge is still marked in Smoots.

overall_summary: This is a clean, fast visual explanation with a strong premise-to-proof structure: body-length measuring, the Smoot name reveal, then a real bridge marking. The sole substantive gap is that it never supplies the total measurement the setup makes viewers expect. Add that number without disturbing the final photo payoff.
